A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UBA scheduling work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison after matching relocated material and inspecting rendered figures.

before.justification: V3 reports original vision-classification experiments, OLMo training and downstream evaluations, and scheduling ablations in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: V4 retains original vision and language experiments and adds an initial-learning-rate sensitivity experiment in Appendix E.8.

M1.justification: The optimization formulation, numerical solution and curve-fitting procedure, UBA schedule in Equation (5), and multi-phase extension are unchanged. The added PyTorch implementation description documents the existing method.

E1.justification: The CIFAR10, CIFAR100, ImageNet, and OLMo training/evaluation tasks remain unchanged. Removing VGG16 and adding a learning-rate sweep change model configurations and experimental settings within retained data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Retained comparisons use SS, CS, CLR, 1C, BT, and REX; the 300M OLMo comparison still uses CS, BT, and REX. The new learning-rate study reuses these baselines. Describing BT as equivalent to linear decay clarifies the existing comparator.

E3.justification: V4 removes the VGG16 evaluation configuration. Appendix Table 7 changes CIFAR100–ResNet34 budget labels from 30/60/120 to 75/150/300 epochs, matching labels already present in v3 Table 2; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. New Appendix E.8 tests initial rates 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001 using fewer, unspecified epochs.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.8/Table 11 examines sensitivity to initial learning rate across UBA and all six baselines on CIFAR100–ResNet34. Existing optimizer and φ analyses remain unchanged. The multi-phase analysis moves from E.8/Table 11 to E.9/Table 12 without substantive revision.

E5.justification: V4 introduces error bars throughout the main vision comparisons in Tables 2 and 7. Appendix E.4 newly reports independent runs, including two for ImageNet, and E.8 reports three runs for the new sensitivity study. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting beyond the retained curve-fitting analysis. However, the new error-bar statistic is undefined, and checklist item 7 contradicts these disclosures by describing single-run reporting.

E6.justification: The primary vision results are substantially replaced, the VGG16 result block is removed, and Table 11 adds learning-rate-sweep results. For CIFAR10 at 300 epochs, reported UBA/BT accuracies change from 95.74/95.55 to 95.65/95.68, reversing their nominal ranking. The new auxiliary experiment reports 79.02 for UBA versus 78.53 for BT at learning rate 0.1. OLMo results and retained ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, optimization problems, propositions, convergence theorem, assumptions, and derivations in Section 3 and Appendices A–D are unchanged. Added prose about worst-case optimization restates the existing reasoning.

C1.justification: V4 adds negligible computational overhead as an explicit advantage in the introduction, contribution list, and conclusion. The abstract and principal claims about unified scheduling, theoretical grounding, and performance across tasks and budgets remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly recognizes that schedules can have different optimal initial learning rates, motivating the additional comparison. Checklist item 10 also acknowledges unexamined computational costs from suboptimal hyperparameter selection. Existing explanations involving preconditioning, optimization difficulty, and limitations of automatic φ selection remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 newly documents inheritance from PyTorch's LRScheduler class and compatibility with torch.optim optimizers, and describes the auxiliary learning-rate search. The repository link, hardware descriptions, software versions, and retained implementation settings are unchanged; the auxiliary experiment's exact epoch count remains unspecified.

R1.justification: The cited works, Section 2, and Appendix F retain the same research positioning and discussion of earlier scheduling and budgeted-training approaches.

P1.justification: V4 adds a NeurIPS checklist, funding acknowledgments, and the new experimental subsection, alongside limited explanatory additions and heading edits. The conference footer replaces the preprint notice. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 changes from side-by-side dataset columns to stacked dataset blocks. Table 7 is restructured with error-bar entries and removal of the VGG16 block; a new Table 11 is added, and the multi-phase table becomes Table 12. Existing figures retain their substantive visual content, with local reflow and relocation.

improvement.justification: The added learning-rate sweep addresses a relevant fairness concern in schedule comparisons, while the revised vision tables provide variability information absent from v3. These offer a limited overall improvement in empirical support. The gains are constrained by lost VGG16 evidence, undefined error bars, and the contradiction between repeated-run disclosures in Appendix E and single-run reporting in checklist item 7.
